Job Description:
Waterfronts Practice Leader

Position Overview

Kingfisher Recruiting has been hired to find a Director of Coastal Engineering and Waterfronts to serve as the strategic, technical, and operational head of the client’s waterfronts and coastal engineering practice. This executive-level leader is responsible for defining the long-term vision of the practice, developing new markets, elevating technical excellence, and guiding multidisciplinary teams in delivering innovative and resilient waterfront solutions. The Practice Leader is a key member of the firm’s leadership team and acts as both a thought leader and a growth catalyst within the industry. This individual will help launch a new office in Louisiana and establish a permanent location in the area.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Vision
Develop and implement the strategic plan for the Waterfronts Practice, aligning with firmwide goals.
Identify emerging market trends in coastal resilience, sustainable waterfront redevelopment, port/marina planning, and marine infrastructure.
Set direction for service offerings, technical capabilities, and geographic expansion.
Champion innovation, digital transformation, and best practices within the practice.

Practice Operations & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, staffing plans, revenue forecasting, and financial performance oversight.
Establish practice-wide quality standards, design procedures, and technical workflows.
Monitor key performance indicators and operational efficiency to ensure best-in-class delivery.
Coordinate resource allocation across regions and project teams to optimize utilization and expertise.

Technical Oversight & Excellence

Serve as senior technical authority for waterfront, marina, and coastal engineering projects.
Provide high-level review and approval of design approaches, engineering calculations, and deliverables.
Guide technical strategy surrounding coastal processes, structural systems, geomorphology, resilience, and nature-based shoreline solutions.
Oversee complex permitting and regulatory pathways at federal, state, and local levels.

Market Leadership & Business Development

Develop strategic relationships with clients, agencies, and consultants.
Lead business development initiatives, major pursuits, and proposal strategies.
Position the firm as a leader in waterfront and coastal engineering through conferences, publications, and industry involvement.
Drive diversification of services and entry into new coastal and marine markets.

Team Leadership, Culture & Development

Build, guide, and mentor a high-performing team of engineers, planners, designers, and project managers.
Foster a culture of collaboration, creativity, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Develop career paths, succession planning, and talent retention strategies for the Waterfronts Practice.
Promote cross-discipline collaboration across the firm to support integrated project delivery.

Qualifications

Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Coastal, Civil, Structural, or Marine Engineering.
15+ years of experience in waterfront, coastal, or marine engineering with increasing leadership responsibilities.
Professional Engineer (PE) license required; additional credentials (e.g., D.PE, PMP, CFM) are desired.
Proven success leading practice groups, business units, or major market sectors.
Strong portfolio of successfully delivered waterfront, marina, or coastal infrastructure projects.
Demonstrated ability to win work, build client relationships, and drive revenue growth.
Deep technical expertise and strong understanding of regulatory and permitting landscapes.

Skills & Core Competencies

Visionary, strategic leader with entrepreneurial mindset.
Strong business acumen and financial management capabilities.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and client engagement skills.
Proven ability to influence, inspire, and develop teams.
High-level decision-making and problem-solving abilities.
Commitment to resilience, sustainability, and innovation in coastal environments.

Working Conditions

Primarily office-based leadership role with periodic travel for client meetings, conferences, project sites, and regional practice oversight.
Occasional field visits to waterfront, marina, or coastal project sites, sometimes under variable conditions.

jobs.description:
Description

How would you like to be a part of Earth’s most customer-centric company? You would work with teams of front-line responders who support the operations of some of the world’s most powerful data centers. Our Data Center Engineering Operations team maintain and operate our critical infrastructure systems so that they are prepared to stand up against any situation.

AWS has the world’s largest cloud computing portfolio. As an Amazonian you will work in some of the most sophisticated, safe, and secure data centers in the world. Our Chief Engineers (CE) help keep them that way by working with the brightest minds from around the globe to help test and implement the newest technology and work practices to meet the demands of a changing market.

We have a passion for learning and evolving, it’s how we have helped define ourselves as leaders in the industry. Let’s work hard, have fun, and make history!

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities

Act as the primary escalation point for all facilities-related issues. Oversee operation and management of routine and emergency services on a variety of critical systems such as: switchgear, generators, UPS systems, power distribution equipment, chillers, cooling towers, computer room air handlers, building monitoring systems, etc.
Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures, and troubleshooting of facility within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA).
Provide training and guidance to Engineering Operations Technicians and responsible for working with Facility Manager (FM) to set team culture.
Create and deploy new standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians, Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams
May assist in the build out of new facilities and assist in projects to increase current facility efficiency
Working outside of normal business hours for routine maintenance as required, including responding to out-of-hours emergency calls.
Communicate complex technical information to a non-technical audience.
Work with IT managers and other business leaders to coordinate projects, manage capacity, and optimize plant safety, performance, reliability and efficiency
Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendor and Amazon staff
Establish building performance benchmarks, conduct analyses, and prepare reports on all aspects of the critical facility operations and maintenance.
Utilize Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook and other basic administrative tools to perform day to day tasks

Physical Requirements

Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

A day in the life

This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including electrical support equipment that supports servers that must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. Equipment will include but is not limited to stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

The CE directs, trains and supports technicians in their role of providing hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. Implementation and execution of site/equipment-specific training exercises is also expected. They manage projects from conception to completion. These projects involve independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, processing, and finance in both local and global settings. The CE will be tasked with creating and delivering on key milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities.

About The Team

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel experience
Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
3+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance experience — OR — 3+ years of electrical facilities maintenance experience and 2+ year of mechanical facilities maintenance experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center engineering or operations
Experience in construction, or experience in project management
Experience leading technical teams through daily operations and maintenance evolutions
Can work in an environment that involves walking, stooping, bending, and climbing to access equipment

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

Our Mission and Opportunity

Early education is one of the most important determinants of childhood outcomes, a critical support for working families, and a $175B market that remains underserved by modern technology. Brightwheel is the largest, fastest growing, and most loved platform in early ed, trusted by millions of educators and families every day. We are a three-time Cloud 100 company, backed by top investors including Addition, Bessemer, Emerson Collective, Lowercase Capital, Notable Capital, and Mark Cuban.

Our Team

Our team is passionate, talented, and customer-focused. We embody our Leadership Principles in our work and culture. We are a distributed team with remote employees across every US time zone, as well as select offices in the US and internationally.

About The Role

In this role, you will lead a team building AI-powered systems for brightwheel’s go-to-market organization. This is a hands-on, cross-functional role: you’ll lead discovery, prototype workflows, and validate them with internal users rather than wait for perfectly defined requirements or dedicated Product and Design support. You’ll work directly with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Operations, and Data to turn ambiguous business problems into reliable products and workflows. The work spans internal products, Salesforce and data integrations, evaluation systems, and customer-facing automation.

You’ll use metrics to decide where to invest, stay close enough to architecture and implementation to form an independent view, and step into prototypes or critical-path code when it helps the team move faster. You won’t wait for perfect requirements: you’ll create clarity, make tradeoffs explicit, and stay accountable through production.

What You’ll Do

Lead a full-stack engineering team from problem definition through production, measurement, and iteration.
Translate company goals into clear outcomes, investment choices, and a credible execution plan.
Set the engineering strategy for quality, reliability, security, privacy, and operational health.
Ship AI-powered products and change how the team works with AI—not just add AI features.
Hire and develop strong engineers, set a clear bar, and act when the team or an individual is below it.
Make capacity, dependencies, forecasts, and risks visible early.
Work directly with GTM and Operations leaders to identify the real problem, map the workflow, prototype a usable solution, and define how success will be measured before scaling.
Build internal products and AI workflows that improve revenue, conversion, productivity, or quality; measure adoption and results.
Own cross-system execution across Salesforce, data, product, and AI services, with clear dependencies and decision rights.

You may be a good fit if you

Have led an engineering team that delivered measurable customer or business results.
Have the technical depth to challenge architecture, product, data, reliability, and operational decisions without taking the work away from the team.
Have set engineering strategy and made explicit investment and prioritization choices.
Have shipped an AI-powered product or workflow to production and can explain the measurable result.
Have hired and developed strong engineers, built succession, and handled performance issues directly.
Have built trusted partnerships across Product, Design, and business teams while representing a clear Engineering point of view.

Strong candidates may also have

Experience in vertical SaaS, education, fintech, healthcare, CRM, ecommerce, or another operations-heavy domain.
Led a material change in product direction, architecture, or operating model.
Built production AI products, agents, evaluation systems, or automation.
Experience leading engineering for internal business functions and working directly with senior stakeholders.
Strong product intuition and UX empathy; can represent Product and Design for small bets and fast iterations when dedicated support is limited.
Experience connecting CRM, data, integration, and AI systems into reliable workflows that move a business metric.

Technology

Backend: Python with FastAPI and asynchronous workers; React with TypeScript.
Data and systems: PostgreSQL, Redshift, DynamoDB, Airflow, Salesforce, and service integrations.
Cloud: AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and production observability.
AI and automation: foundation models, evaluation and orchestration tooling, vector search, and modern AI coding tools.

Description

The AWS data catalog is how customers find, understand, and govern their data on AWS. The AWS Glue Data Catalog is the metadata layer beneath AWS analytics. It holds the schemas, table definitions, and partitions that Athena, EMR, Redshift, Glue, and SageMaker need to plan and execute a query, which puts it in the data path of nearly every analytical workload our customers run, and its crawlers are how a large share of that metadata gets discovered and kept current in the first place. Alongside it, AWS Lake Formation governs fine-grained access to that data, and Amazon DataZone provides the business context, discovery, and lineage (domains, projects, and data products) that make a data estate comprehensible to the people and applications using it. Together these three services serve customers of every size, from day-one startups to the largest enterprises in the world, and hold the definitive record of the data those customers store in Amazon S3 and query with our engines. We are investing heavily to make working with that data dramatically simpler for customers, and to ensure the catalog operates at the hyperscale we expect AI agents, rather than people, to drive as they become the primary consumers of enterprise data. Catalogs have become the control point for enterprise data and AI, and we are at the very beginning of building the one customers standardize on.

As a Director of Software Development for the AWS Catalog organization, you will lead a group of top talent building the metadata, governance, and discovery layer for all data on AWS. You will own the AWS Glue Data Catalog and its crawlers, AWS Lake Formation, and Amazon DataZone, and you will drive the roadmap and deliver on three fronts at once: building a foundation that operates at a scale and request rate well beyond what any catalog handles today, with the availability and latency that every analytics service above you depends on; making governance simpler and stronger for customers who have to know and prove who can see what across a large data estate; and making the catalog the layer that AI agents reason through, with the discovery, semantic search, and business metadata that let an agent find the right data without being told where it lives. You will do this while holding a deep commitment to open standards, building on Apache Iceberg and the Iceberg REST Catalog and interoperating with third-party catalogs rather than locking customers in. You'll lead multiple engineering teams through managers across geographic locations, and you'll spearhead new technologies that change what a catalog is capable of. You'll be a leader in the business as well, owning the financial health and growth of your services. You'll personally engage with C-suite customers to represent AWS's data catalog strategy.

Success in this role requires a leader experienced in establishing and building relationships with a wide range of peers, including senior AWS executives, customers at all levels of experience and responsibility, deeply technical software and systems engineers within the team, and internal organizations. Because the catalog sits between storage and every analytics and AI service, this role rewards a leader who builds strong partnerships across engineering teams and brings them along behind a shared technical direction. The director of national development has a primary responsibility for the strategic solicitation of individual gifts for the Case School of Engineering. Develop strategies to build a strong relationship with corporation and foundation partners, which may include the dean, associate dean and other senior staff of the school, president, provost and senior vice president of development and university relations. Develop major gift strategies that leverage corporation and foundation partnerships with on campus activities. (10%)
Serve as a member of the development staff and assist with the development and implementation of program strategies and overall departmental development plans to fulfill the mission of the school and the university. (10%)
Identify, qualify, recruit, train and manage alumni volunteers as appropriate, who will actively participate in the soliciting of gifts of all levels. Partner with volunteers to engage and cultivate individuals who have capacity to make gifts of $100,000 to $250,000 to the school. (10%)

Provide assistance with other funding priorities as determined by the senior director of national development. (4%)
Perform other duties as assigned by the senior director of national development. (1%)

Department: Frequent contact with dean, associate/assistant deans, department chairs, directors, faculty, students and staff as required to perform essential functions.

University: Contact with the president's office, vice presidents, deans, trustees, alumni, directors of administrative departments, faculty and staff as required to perform essential functions.

External: Daily contact with donors, alumni, foundation representatives, community organizers/advocates, corporate executives and federal, state and local government officials. Contact with visitors, academic boards and organizations as required to perform essential functions.

No direct supervisory responsibility.

About the Opportunity

The company is a national workforce development organization that connects work-authorized, college-educated immigrants to skill-aligned professional employment across the United States. It addresses a significant economic inefficiency: millions of highly educated, work-authorized immigrants are underemployed, representing substantial forgone wages and untapped productivity for the economy. The organization's model has proven effective, with jobseekers entering programs earning an average of $9,000 per year and being placed in roles averaging $67,000 per year. To date, the organization has supported an estimated 35,000 job placements, contributing billions in earnings to the U.S. economy. The organization is data-driven, economically accountable, and built for scale. It is committed to leveraging AI to its fullest potential, driving operational efficiency, jobseeker readiness, and national economic impact. The organization operates nationally, partnering with leading employers, workforce agencies, and policymakers to ensure that global talent becomes an American advantage.

This role is responsible for building and leading the organization's technology strategy and infrastructure to support both internal operations and externally facing digital products. This includes staff-facing technology as well as the technical infrastructure that enables jobseeker and partner experiences. This leader partners closely with the CEO, President, and executive leadership to ensure technology is a strategic enabler of the organization's mission, helping the organization transition towards an AI and product-first model while maintaining strong operational excellence, security, reliability, and scalable delivery practices. The organization will integrate AI into all aspects to drive operational excellence, improve jobseeker opportunities and outcomes, and this role will help lead these efforts. The VP of Technology is expected to be both strategic and execution-oriented: setting direction, making tradeoffs clear, and delivering consistently across teams.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Strategy & AI Infrastructure
Own the organization's technology strategy across staff infrastructure and jobseeker/partner-facing products, ensuring both are secure, scalable, cost-effective, and aligned to mission outcomes.
Build and maintain a multi-year technology roadmap covering staff infrastructure and IT operations, data systems and reporting, Salesforce/platform evolution, core digital products (jobseeker portal, online learning, partner tools), and integrations/interoperability across systems.
Translate organizational strategy into a sequenced plan with clear timelines, dependencies, resource needs, and success measures.
Provide clear tradeoffs and recommendations to the Executive Leadership Team on what to prioritize, defer, or stop based on capacity and impact.
Support sprint planning, release planning, and other Agile ceremonies.

Product & Engineering Partnership (Jobseeker + Partner Products)
